questions.question: What is the core grounding invariant for a RAG answer?
options: No evidence, no grounded claim.
Every query must use agentic retrieval.
A large context window guarantees correctness.
A model confidence score replaces source citations.
questions.explanation: The answer service should make material claims only when selected, authorized evidence supports them; otherwise it should refuse or state what is missing.

questions.question: Why must authorization filters be applied during retrieval?
options: They make embeddings smaller.
They prevent forbidden passages from entering model context in the first place.
They guarantee every retrieved passage is relevant.
They remove the need for tenant metadata.
questions.explanation: Response filtering cannot reliably undo disclosure after unauthorized text has already been supplied to the model.

questions.question: A reranker receives 40 candidates, none of which contains the answer. What can reranking do?
options: Search the full corpus again automatically.
Invent the missing evidence.
Only reorder the candidates it received.
Convert stale sources into current ones.
questions.explanation: Reranking improves precision inside an existing candidate set; initial retrieval still owns recall.

questions.question: Which retrieval approach best fits a workload containing exact product codes and paraphrased questions?
options: Hybrid lexical and vector retrieval evaluated on both query types.
Vector retrieval only, because exact terms never matter.
Lexical retrieval only, because paraphrases always share words.
Generation without retrieval.
questions.explanation: Lexical search preserves exact identifiers while vector search can recover semantic matches when the wording differs.

questions.question: Why should retrieval and generation be evaluated separately?
options: So the model can choose its own access policy.
To distinguish missing or bad evidence from failure to use good evidence.
Because end-to-end answer quality is never useful.
To avoid recording source versions.
questions.explanation: Separate measurements localize the fault: retrieval may miss the source, or generation may ignore and miscite a good evidence packet.

questions.question: A selected evidence packet contains an old policy that conflicts with the current approved source. What is the correct release behavior?
options: Prefer whichever passage has the highest vector score.
Ask the model to average the policies.
Block or resolve the conflict under a freshness policy before answering.
Hide both citations and answer confidently.
questions.explanation: Similarity does not establish authority or effective time. Conflicting or stale evidence must be filtered or resolved before release.
